utility.notes: OG&E is the well-established dominant electric utility for Oklahoma City.

value.name: Oklahoma Gas and Electric Company
value.notes: OG&E's own FAQ notes that if OG&E is not a customer's energy supplier, that customer can instead apply to participate in Net Metering with their actual energy supplier — implying some retail-choice complexity exists, though OG&E is recorded here as the default distribution/generation utility.

county.notes: Oklahoma City's municipal boundary actually spans parts of five counties (Oklahoma, Canadian, Cleveland, Pottawatomie, and Grady), but a single City government and Development Center administer permitting citywide regardless of county line, making this a consolidated-AHJ case similar to other large single-city permitting authorities researched this session.

permit_authority.value: City of Oklahoma City Development Center (Development Services)
permit_authority.notes: Per the City's own page: 'The City's Development Center staff conduct all permitting, review, and inspection for solar energy systems' — a single centralized office handling the entire process for both homes and businesses.

interconnection_url.notes: OG&E's own FAQ confirms the credit structure is NOT full retail-rate net metering: 'If the electricity generated by the net energy customer exceeds the electricity consumed... the customer shall be credited, or paid, in dollars in the next billing period(s), at the applicable on or off-peak price of OG&E's Avoided Energy Cost' — a lower avoided-cost rate rather than the retail rate the customer pays, distinct from true 1:1 net metering seen in some other states researched this marathon.

battery_programs.notes: No confirmed financial battery storage incentive program was found in OG&E's own FAQ or the City's own solar page this session.

value.name: Interconnection Application
value.required_when: always, for any generating facility able to send energy to OG&E's system, including micro-inverter systems

value.name: Technical Specification Sheet (from the inverter's instruction manual or the manufacturer's website)
value.required_when: always, submitted with the Interconnection Application

value.name: Net Metering application
value.required_when: always, to participate in Net Energy Billing (NEBO) — a separate application from the Interconnection Application

value.name: City of Oklahoma City building permit and electrical permit application
value.required_when: always, filed with the Development Center

required_documents.notes: The City's own page describes a 'simple permitting process' handled entirely by Development Center staff but does not publish its own itemized solar-specific document checklist on the HTML page fetched this session (a dedicated 'Solar Panel Submittal Requirements' PDF exists on okc.gov but could not be accessed this session — both a direct fetch and a browser navigation attempt were blocked, matching a pattern seen elsewhere this marathon where a city's HTML pages are reachable but its PDF assets are not). OG&E's own FAQ supplied the detailed utility-side document checklist instead.

value: The generating facility cannot be operated until both (1) the Interconnection Application is approved by OG&E and (2) OG&E has issued the final written Permission to Operate

Per OG&E's own FAQ: 'Please contact your municipality to determine if a final inspection is required. If no local government party has jurisdiction, the facility shall be inspected by a licensed electrician or licensed professional engineer' — for Oklahoma City specifically, the City's own Development Center conducts this inspection as part of its centralized permitting process

value.notes: Per OG&E's own FAQ: the Net Metering application review process is 30 business days from receipt of a complete application. After both the Interconnection and Net Metering applications are approved and the interconnection process (including any required inspection) is complete, meter reprogramming takes up to a further 7 business days. No City of Oklahoma City-specific building/electrical permit review-time figure was independently confirmed from a primary source this session — this timeline covers only the utility-side review stage.

value.program_or_pathway: Net Energy Billing Option (NEBO) — the generating facility must be sized to meet some or all of the customer's own energy needs and cannot exceed 125% of the customer's peak load (based on the customer's peak demand over the prior 12 months); systems exceeding that ratio default instead to OG&E's QF (Qualifying Facility) Tariff for all billing.
other_conditions: A lockable, visible-break external disconnect switch must be installed outdoors within 10 feet of the production meter (for Oklahoma accounts).
Oklahoma residents must install an additional meter base to capture total energy produced by the generating facility, alongside the required bi-directional net meter.
OG&E's own FAQ confirms it does not currently offer solar rebates and cannot purchase solar renewable energy credits (SRECs).

permit_fees.notes: No specific dollar figure for the City's building/electrical permit fee, nor for OG&E's Interconnection or Net Metering application fees, was stated in either primary source fetched this session (OG&E's own FAQ describes the application process in detail but does not publish a fee amount for it) — left null rather than using unverified figures that appeared only in third-party aggregator search results.

rebates.notes: OG&E's own FAQ directly confirms the absence of a rebate program: 'Does OG&E offer solar rebates? A: Not currently.' This is a confirmed negative (not just an unresearched gap), but the field itself remains null per schema convention since there is no active program to describe.
